snippet.title: HEAL from The Princess of Wales | Trailer
snippet.description:
Introducing Heal, a deeply personal new documentary from The Princess of Wales, exploring life beyond diagnosis and the many ways people find comfort, strength and hope in the face of serious illness.
 
Through this documentary, The Princess hopes to help others navigate diagnosis, recovery and life beyond cancer and transform access to holistic cancer care which supports wellbeing, resilience and quality of life during and after diagnosis.
 
All funds received through the documentary's distribution have been directed to The Royal Marsden Cancer Charity to help people living with and beyond cancer. To support, visit www.royalmarsden.org/princessofwales
 
Heal will be broadcast in the following regions:
• United Kingdom - BBC iPlayer from 12pm and BBC One, 6:40pm GMT, Sunday 29 November
• United States - NBC, 8pm ET/PT; Bravo, 11.30pm ET/PT, Monday 30 November and streaming on Peacock from Tuesday 1 December
• Australia - Channel 9 and 9Now, 7.30pm AEDT, Tuesday 1 December
• Canada - CTV, 10pm ET and Noovo 7.30pm ET, Monday 7 December, and streaming on Crave from Tuesday 8 December
 
Heal was produced by Will Warr (Detail Films):
• Director – Benji Jackson
• Director of Photography / Editor - Will Warr 
• Production Support – Helen Thomas
• Trailer Editor – Toby Dashwood
• Second Camera – Benji Jackson and Doug Cock
• Original Score – Erland Cooper
• Sound Design – Hugo Ellingham
• Colourist – Dan Moran

More about Moon Sweepers (from Steam):

The Moon is covered in dust. The Lunar Surface Department (LSD) has sent you and your crew to clean it up. Unfortunately, the budget only covered a toothbrush.

Collect lunar dust, sell and use the earnings to buy better tools and upgrade your equipment. Turn an underfunded cleanup mission into a growing operation, one painfully small brushstroke at a time.

Team up in online co-op lobbies of up to 16 players. Spread out to cover more ground or tackle the same area together. There’s enough dust to keep everyone busy. Whether everyone actually works is another matter.

Fill your storage with lunar dust, deliver it to a depot and launch shipments to get paid. Spend your earnings on new cleaning tools and increased carrying capacity so you can take on bigger jobs between deliveries.

Watch dusty terrain turn clean with every pass. Track your progress across the lunar surface, place depots near your work and put cleaning vehicles to use as your operation grows.

Stop being lazy, you’ve got whole Moon to clean. Better get started.

Lyrics:

[Intro: Shaggy & Rayvon]
Now this one's dedicated to all the youths who want to say nice things to all dem girls
(Heh, heh, heh, shooby dooby dooby doo boy, shooby doo)
Treat her like diamonds and pearls

(Now) Now this is Rayvon and Shaggy with a combination you can't miss

Ah ah, wah wah wah

Girl, you're my angel, you're my darling angel
Closer than my peeps you are to me, baby (Tell them)
Shorty, you're my angel, you're my darling angel
Girl, you're my friend when I'm in need, lady

Life is one big party when you're still young
But who's gonna have your back when it's all done? (Yeah)
It's all good when you're little, you have pure fun
Can't be a fool, son, what about the long run?
Looking back, Shorty always mention
Said me not giving her much attention (Yeah)
She was there through my incarceration
I wanna show the nation my appreciation

Girl, you're my friend when I'm in need, lady

Uh, uh

snippet.title: Season 25 - Shotta's.
snippet.description:
"Season 25 - Shotta's" (S25 Shottas) blends hard-hitting underground trap production with deep 808 basslines, crisp hi-hats, and a dark, hypnotic synth loop. Anchored by a catchy, repetitive hook, Season 25 delivers raw, unfiltered rap verses with a relentless cadence that builds high-octane, late-night club energy (1:40). From the punchy drum patterns to the confident vocal delivery, this track captures an authentic street-level sound built for heavy playlist rotation.
RapXtreme Newsletter: https://rapxtreme.substack.com
Stream: https://open.spotify.com/track/1ApUYfDejOBvrTnar2Wyf3?autoplay_ok=1

Support the Artist
https://open.spotify.com/artist/1WtceoonufhxRc6AnUSbat

“Shotta’s.” carries a bold, restless, and confrontational mood, mixing late-night club energy with the frustration of watching a friend remain in a damaging relationship. The repeated advice to “let that [woman] go” gives the track a direct, exasperated tone, while references to bottles, dancing, models, and drinking until morning create a celebratory nightlife backdrop.

Lyrically, it moves between relationship advice and confident flexing. Lines about getting checks, working for money, driving a car with hydraulics, and being surrounded by his “shottas” highlight ambition, success, and loyalty. ✯ WHO WE ARE -
RespawnTV is a hub for gamers and creators to showcase their most entertaining and unforgettable gameplay moments. Unlike channels that simply repost clips, we focus on producing unique content with engaging commentary and polished editing.

Hosted by me (Sid), each video includes thoughtful commentary that adds context and entertainment to every clip. Creating a single video takes significant effort — from gathering clips (around 4–5 hours), writing scripts (2–3 hours), recording voiceovers (about 1 hour), to editing (10–12 hours), making the total production time roughly 20–24 hours.

snippet.title: GTA 6 Feels Like Something's Off...
snippet.description:
GTA 6 has a 99 on Metacritic and the best looking world Rockstar has ever made. But eight hours in, I can't name one moment I'd tell a mate about, and I feel nothing for Jason and Lucia. It feels like watching a movie instead of playing a game. So I went through the player reviews, what Asmongold, Lacy and other streamers have said, and the clips everyone is sharing, to work out what's actually missing and why the man who wrote Trevor, Niko and Arthur Morgan might be the answer.

Do you feel connected to Jason and Lucia, or does it feel like you're just watching them? Tell me in the comments.

snippet.title: GTA 6: How to Find Treasure in Scuba Mission (EASY)
snippet.description:
How to find the treasure in Island Dreams in GTA 6. In this video I show you exactly where to search for treasure near the wreck in Kenton's scuba diving mission, with every treasure location marked on the map.

Island Dreams is a Chapter 1 story mission in GTA 6 where Jason takes a bachelor party on a scuba dive for Kenton in Key Lento. Once you escort the bachelor party through the trench, you get the objective "Search for treasure near the wreck." The shipwreck area all looks the same, so it's easy to get lost. Use the metal detector, stay in the marked search area, and follow the spots I show in this video. After that, rescue Dobbs and escort the bachelor party back to the boat to finish the mission.

snippet.title: GTA 6: FREE Supercars With NO Tracker + Paul Walker's Car (Locations)
snippet.description:
The best cars to steal in GTA 6 Chapter 2: two FREE supercars with NO tracker ($33,000 and $32,205) and Paul Walker's Fast & Furious car, with exact locations.

Most supercars in GTA 6 are keyless, and you don't get the Key Cloner until Chapter 3. These 3 cars don't need it. For each one: the exact location, how to steal it, and what it sells for vs. what it costs to register (real scan-card numbers).

0:00 The gold Lamborghini you can't have
0:36 The "Bugatti on a trailer" myth
0:55 How to read a car scan
1:19 #3 Paul Walker's Penumbra FF
2:18 #2 Purple Drank Emerus
3:17 #1 Royal Ruby Emerus
4:32 Scoreboard

QUICK LIST
• Scan every car with your phone first. ACCESS "Key Cloner" = walk away for now. TRACKER "None" = nobody's coming for it.
• #3 Maibatsu '97 Penumbra FF (Paul Walker's car): mansion garage on Vespucci Island, Neptune Circle. Locked + alarmed, no tracker. Use the slim jim (Moses, Chapter 2), don't smash the window. Sells $1,210, registers for $6,750. Keep it.
• #2 Progen Purple Drank Emerus: inside a shipping container at Chatfield Storage & Logistics (Vice City docks). Armed guards. Unlocked, no tracker. Sells $32,205, registers for $29,900.
• #1 Progen Royal Ruby Emerus: Vespucci Mansion (Vespucci Island), heavily guarded, go at night. Unlocked, no tracker. Sells $33,000, registers for $29,900.
• Both Emerus spots are on your map under Robberies → Other Criminals.
• Can't afford to register yet? Park it in a garage (Persistence Road Garage is $9,500). Cars parked there stay safe until you take them out.
• Not worth the trip yet: the gold Lustrous Toros (Casanova Island) and the Gold Rush Tempesta (Washington Beach garage) both need the Key Cloner and have advanced trackers. And the viral "Bugatti on a trailer" at Boone Speedway was a $1,430 buggy when we went.

Numbers are the on-screen scan values from my playthrough. Spawns can change.
All gameplay is my own.

snippet.title: I Investigated GTA 6's Secret Underwater Caves
snippet.description:
Get 10% off all GamerSupps products with this link: https://gamersupps.gg/drmod

GTA 6's underwater caves are both beautiful and absolutely terrifying...

In this video, I explore GTA 6's hidden underwater cave systems, discovering just how much lies beneath the surface of Leonida. What begins as a peaceful exploration of Emerald Springs, a stunning national park filled with crystal-clear turquoise waters, wildlife and natural springs, quickly turns into one of the most terrifying experiences I've had in GTA6.

Inspired by real-life Florida locations like Devil's Den, these underwater caves contain mysterious tunnels, dangerous passages and chilling warning signs telling divers not to go any further.

But curiosity got the better of me, and I decided to investigate just how deep these caves really go...

As I ventured further underground, visibility disappeared, the tunnels became increasingly confusing, and I eventually found myself completely lost, desperately searching for a way out before running out of oxygen.

From beautiful natural springs to terrifying underwater cave diving, GTA 6's world is full of incredible details, hidden locations and unexpected discoveries.

snippet.title: You Built a Bunker to Last 5 Years. You Stayed for 50
snippet.description:
You built a bunker for one person and five years. Then the war never ended — and you stayed underground for fifty.
 
A bunker survival story animation about one man, one room under a barn, and the war that kept going above him. Armies dig trenches across your field, every farmhouse for thirty miles burns, and nuclear war turns the country into a map nobody can read. Below, a single shelter slowly grows into an underground village of 34 people — a mechanic named Nolan, a woman named Lena, a son born twelve feet under the ground. And for fifty years, nobody touches your hatch.
 
Everything about how the bunker works is kept real: how fallout fades, how long diesel, filters and LED bulbs actually last, how much heat a crowded shelter makes, how you grow food with no sun, and what fifty years underground does to a body and a mind.
 
Would you have opened the hatch? Tell me in the comments.

snippet.title: GTA 6 Deserves Its Brutal Metacritic Score

Critics gave Grand Theft Auto 6 a near-perfect 99 on Metacritic, while the paying public handed it a brutal 5.6 user score. In this video, I break down the exact reasons why so many longtime fans and paying customers are furious with GTA 6 after waiting thirteen years. From shipping an empty box with a download code and locking consoles to 30 FPS in 2026, to trading chaotic sandbox freedom for slow hyperrealism, a domestic storyline, and impossible corporate hype here is why GTA 6 earned every point of its low user score.

snippet.title: GTA 6 Is Already Falling Apart
snippet.description:
GTA 6 got a 99 from critics and a 3.7 from players. Here is everything that went wrong in its first week: the 30 FPS cap on every console, the crashes Rockstar hasn’t addressed, the $80 box with no disc and sometimes no code, GTA+ inside the single-player story, and the fights over Lucia that pulled in Asmongold, NickEh30, xQc and TimTheTatman.

The PlayStation Network outage hours before launch. Digital Foundry’s numbers on PS5, PS5 Pro and Series S. The boxes that arrived with missing or used codes. The subscription perks in story mode. The cut content, no PC and no GTA Online. The tribunal over the 31 fired union members that closed two days before launch, and the Firaxis layoffs. And $3.79 billion on day one anyway. Every problem ends up on the board as CONFIRMED, OVERBLOWN or STILL OPEN.

Claims from posts and creators are labelled as claims; legal claims are allegations unless a court has ruled. Nothing here says anyone committed a crime.

Sources: Rockstar Games and Take-Two statements, Digital Foundry, Metacritic, OpenCritic, Kotaku, VGC, IGN, Dexerto, IBTimes, LADbible, GAMINGbible, GTA BOOM, Shacknews, Rolling Stone, TMZ / New York Post, Engadget, Newsweek, Axios, The Daily Beast, Downdetector, HotHardware, Tom’s Hardware, Notebookcheck, Ampere Analysis, Sensor Tower, CNBC, CBS, CNN, BBC News, Variety, Yahoo Finance, Box Office Mojo, Fortune, Polygon, PC Gamer, The Guardian, IWGB, Hardware Unboxed, Philip DeFranco, Asmongold, TimTheTatman, NickEh30, xQc, Lord Frogmire, penguinz0, JoeFromSeattle, Mannix, SKizzle, Clownfish TV, IShowSpeed and gameplay by MKIceAndFire and others. All clips are used for commentary and criticism.
